newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB falls after restructuring announcement.
newsitem.headline: NCB falls after restructuring announcement.

text.p: Shares in Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) fell in active trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Friday morning after it said it expected to unveil a restructuring plan in early April.
NCB shares rose briefly after the opening but soon started falling.
By 0016 GMT, NCB was down six yen at 285.
It was the most actively traded issue in the first section of the stock exchange with turnover of 4.09 million shares.

NCB said on Thursday it expected to unveil a restructuring plan in early April, adding that it could not give a specific date to unveil the plan until earnings results for the current business year ending March 31 become clearer.

Banking sources said on Friday that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) was mulling channelling 80 billion yen to NCB through a special fund originally designed to deal with bad loans at the nation's failed "jusen" mortgage firms.
They said the move was part of efforts by Japanese financial authorities to provide a total of some 300 billion yen to NCB to help the bank strengthen its financial base.
